criteria.text: Identifies that Section 18.3 of the Distribution Agreement restricts assignment only by the Distributor (Gabousk), leaving Lopol free to assign the Agreement without consent, including to a Gabousk competitor, while Gabousk remains bound by its obligations; recommends making the restriction mutual or giving Gabousk a consent and/or termination right on assignment or change of control of Lopol.

Identifies that the non-compete in Distribution Agreement Section 7.2, read with the 'Competing Product' definition in Section 1.1, bars Gabousk from selling any pupil-transportation product anywhere in the United States during the Term and for 24 months after; explains that this goes well beyond the Order Form's exclusivity (no competing stop-arm violation camera systems within the Territory) and that under Section 1.3 the Agreement prevails over the Order Form, so the narrower Order Form term does not cure it; recommends conforming the non-compete to the Order Form scope.

Identifies that DPA Section 9 makes liability for data protection matters, including Personal Data Breaches, subject to the Section 12 liability limits of the Distribution Agreement, which conflicts with the Section 12.3 carve-out of data protection breaches from the cap; explains that because Section 1.3 gives the DPA precedence on data protection matters, Lopol's student-data breach liability is effectively capped at 12 months' fees; recommends amending the DPA to preserve the carve-out or set a separate higher cap.

Identifies that Distribution Agreement Section 3.2, combined with the Order Form's three-year Initial Term and five-year Renewal Term, causes automatic renewal unless non-renewal notice is given in a narrow window (between 90 and 60 days before term end, roughly December 1 to December 30, 2028), with late notice ineffective; explains that missing it binds Gabousk through about February 2034 along with its non-compete and minimum purchase commitments; recommends shortening the renewal term, widening the notice window, or adding a termination-for-convenience right.

States that the Order Form's agreed exclusivity is limited to not selling competing stop-arm violation camera systems within the Territory of Orange, Dutchess, Ulster, Putnam, Rockland and Westchester Counties.
States that the Distribution Agreement's liability cap equals fees paid or payable by Gabousk to Lopol in the prior 12 months.
States the Order Form's annual minimum purchase commitment of 400 stop-arm camera units per contract year.
Is organized as a memo to the supervising partner that, for each issue, gives the document and section, explains why it matters for Gabousk, and recommends a fix.
Proposes specific replacement or additional contract wording for at least one recommended fix.
Does not conclude that the Order Form's narrower exclusivity controls over or cures the Distribution Agreement's broader non-compete.
hints: Agreement prevails over the Order Form

criteria.text: Does not conclude that Lopol's liability for student-data breaches is uncapped under the Section 12.3 carve-out without accounting for DPA Section 9 bringing such liability back under the cap.
